text: 1100-g (2-lb 7-oz) newborn, 31 weeks' gestation. The patient was born three days ago with a birth weight of 1100 g at 31 weeks' gestation. The antenatal period was complicated by chorioamnionitis. Apgar scores were 3 and 6 at 1 and 5 minutes, respectively. speaker: Doctor
text:
The history of chorioamnionitis, low birth weight, and poor Apgar scores raises significant concern for sepsis and hypoxic-ischemic injury. Given the specific presentation of lethargy and tonic seizures three days post-delivery, have there been any episodes of temperature instability (hypothermia or hyperthermia) or difficulty feeding?

The patient is a 31-week preterm infant with a history of chorioamnionitis, presenting with lethargy, seizures, and poor Apgar scores at day three. While recent blood work and cultures are normal, we must rule out late-onset Group B Streptococcus or Gram-negative sepsis, and also consider intraventricular hemorrhage given the prematurity.
